info.name: ADD OS — Identity & Content
info.description:
واجهة برمجية (API) لتطبيق ADD OS - تطبيق إدارة المستخدمين والمحتوى

الميزات الرئيسية:
• مصادقة الأعضاء: رقم الهاتف + كلمة المرور
• مصادقة الموظفين: البريد الإلكتروني + كلمة المرور + مصادقة ثنائية
• نظام الخدمات الديناميكي: ADD Core / Experience / Ecosystem

قبل البدء:
1. استورد بيئة العمل المحلية: ADD OS - Local
2. شغل الخادم: php artisan serve --port=8000

نظام الفرع الافتراضي:
يتم تحديد branch_id تلقائياً من الباك اند (ResolveDefaultBranch).
يمكن تحديد فرع محدد عبر هيدر X-Branch-Id أو branch_id صراحةً.

item.name: Member (App)
item.description: Phone + password أ¢â€ â€™ Sanctum bearer token, with a WhatsApp code (mock driver for now) gating sign-up and password recovery.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
MEMBERS ONLY. An operations or admin account cannot sign in or reset a password anywhere in this folder أ¢â‚¬â€‌ those accounts belong to Admin/Auth, behind Fortify's second factor. Tokens minted here carry the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects, so this surface stays sealed off from operations even for someone who is legitimately both.

Two separate journeys, in order.

SIGN UP (once per member): Register أ¢â‚¬â€‌ Send Code أ¢â€ â€™ Register أ¢â‚¬â€‌ Verify & Create. Step 1 validates the whole profile and parks it, so a number that already has an account is refused there with a 422 rather than after the OTP round trip; step 2 then needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` until step 2.

SIGN IN (every time after): Login with phone + password. Refresh Token renews the access token when it expires (60 min) without re-entering the password; Logout ends the session on this device only.

FORGOT IT: Forgot Password أ¢â€ â€™ Reset Password. The reset revokes every token the member holds on every device, and deliberately issues none أ¢â‚¬â€‌ sign in again afterwards.

Register أ¢â‚¬â€‌ Verify & Create, Login and Refresh Token all capture the pair into {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}}. Account Reactivation -- Verify does the same.

DEACTIVATED, WANT BACK IN: Account Reactivation -- Request Code -> Account Reactivation -- Verify. Only works on an account a member deactivated themselves (Member (App)/Account/Deactivate Account) -- a blocked account can't use this; only an admin can reverse a block. Verify signs the member straight back in with a fresh token pair, since a deactivated account holds no live session to return to.

Already signed in and just want a new password without having forgotten the old one? That's Member (App)/Account/Change Password instead -- it proves identity with the current password rather than a code, and only ends every *other* session, not this one.

request.description:
Step 1 of sign-up. Validates the ENTIRE profile first and only then sends the code أ¢â‚¬â€‌ so "this number already has an account", "that email is taken" and "password too short" all come back as 422 here, before you spend a WhatsApp message and an OTP round trip on a sign-up that was never going to succeed.

On success the profile is parked in `pending_registrations` (password already hashed) so step 2 needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` أ¢â‚¬â€‌ an unverified sign-up is never an account. The parked row expires with its code after 5 minutes and is swept hourly by `model:prune`, so abandoning the flow leaves nothing behind and holds no phone number.

Running this again overwrites the parked profile, which is how you correct a typo: fix the field, re-send, use the new code.

There is no `purpose` field أ¢â‚¬â€‌ this endpoint always mints a `registration` code, and Forgot Password always mints a `password_reset` one. A code issued by one is refused by the other with an explicit 422; they are not interchangeable.

Rate-limited (1 per cooldown window per phone per purpose, plus a 10/min per-IP throttle). Code is dispatched via the mock WhatsApp driver أ¢â‚¬â€‌ check storage/logs/laravel.log for the value until a real gateway is wired up.

Step 2 of sign-up, and ACCOUNT CREATION ONLY أ¢â‚¬â€‌ this is no longer the repeat login the old otp/verify was. Returning members use Login.

Just the phone and the code. The profile was validated and parked at step 1, so nothing is re-typed and the password crosses the wire only once. Creates the account, assigns the 'member' role, provisions an empty wallet, and discards the parked row أ¢â‚¬â€‌ all in one transaction.

Returns an access_token + refresh_token pair, both captured automatically. The access token carries the ability `member-app` and nothing more, so it cannot reach /api/v1/admin/* even if the same person is also an operator.

422 "please start signing up again" means there is no parked profile أ¢â‚¬â€‌ step 1 was never run, or it expired along with its code (both last 5 minutes). Re-run step 1.

409 means the number or email was free at step 1 and got claimed in between أ¢â‚¬â€‌ a race, not the normal "already registered" answer, which step 1 gives you as a 422.

Resends the registration OTP to a phone that already has a pending registration (created by **Register â€” Step 1** / Send Code).

Silent on unknown phones (returns 200 with no indication whether the phone has a pending registration).

- **200** â€” Code (re-)sent, or phone has no pending registration (silent).
- **429** â€” Throttled; `retry_after` (seconds) says when to try again.

Use this when the member never received the initial code or it expired.

The everyday sign-in, for MEMBERS ONLY. Returns the same access_token + refresh_token pair sign-up does, both captured automatically. The token carries the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects.

401 is deliberately identical for three different failures أ¢â‚¬â€‌ wrong password, unregistered number, and an account that holds no `member` role (an operations or admin account). Operators sign in at Admin/Auth/Login, behind Fortify's second factor; if this endpoint issued them a token, phone + password alone would reach the operations API and the second factor would be worth nothing. The wording is shared so the response can't be used to work out which numbers have accounts, or which of those belong to staff.

403 means the account is deactivated or blocked; no token is issued and the body names the state.

429 after 5 attempts per minute for this phone+IP combination, with retry_after in the body.

Renews an expired access token without the password. Unauthenticated أ¢â‚¬â€‌ the refresh token in the body IS the credential.

Single use: the token sent here is revoked and the previous access token deleted, so both variables are overwritten with the replacements. Sending the same refresh token twice returns 401.

Also 401 if the refresh token has expired (30 days) or the account was deactivated/blocked in the meantime.

Initiates the password reset flow for a registered member.

- **200** â€” Phone belongs to an active member account; a 6-digit reset code has been sent.
- **422** â€” Phone is not registered with any member account.
- **429** â€” OTP request throttled; `retry_after` (seconds) tells you when to try again.

On 200, proceed to **Verify Password Reset** with the code the member receives.

Verifies the 6-digit code sent by **Forgot Password** and authorizes a password reset server-side.

On success the server records a short-lived authorization on the OTP record â€” no token is returned to the client. Proceed directly to **Reset Password** using the same phone number.

Completes the password reset flow.

The server verifies that the OTP for this phone was verified and authorized within the reset window (controlled by `otp.reset_token_ttl_minutes`). No client-side token is required â€” authorization is held server-side.

After a successful reset all existing tokens for the account are revoked; the member must log in again.

Sends an `account_reactivation` code -- only useful to a phone that belongs to a DEACTIVATED member account (that's Member (App)/Account/Deactivate Account, the self-service action that puts it in this state). Always answers 200 with the same neutral message whether or not that applies, same as Forgot Password -- a 200 here is not confirmation anything was sent.

A blocked account never gets a code here -- reversing a block is admin-only (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). Read the code from storage/logs/laravel.log (mock WhatsApp driver) and paste it into Account Reactivation -- Verify.

Restores the account to `active` and signs it straight back in -- unlike Reset Password, this issues a fresh access_token + refresh_token pair (captured automatically), because a deactivated account has no live session to fall back on; there is no separate Login step afterwards.

The code must have been issued by Account Reactivation -- Request Code. A registration or password-reset code sent here is refused with 422 and a message saying so.
Revokes the current access token. Calling Account/Get Me again afterwards should return 401.
Returns profile, roles, permissions, and active status for the currently authenticated member.

request.description: 403 if the acting member isn't an admin of this specific company. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.
403 if the acting member isn't already an admin of this specific company. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated membership resource.

Gap found in the Task 15 Postman audit. Company-admin only (CompanyPolicy::manageMembers) -- reallocates from the company wallet's general balance, it does not add new money. restricted_space_id is required when category is space_specific and prohibited otherwise; category general is rejected.

Gap found in the Task 15 Postman audit. Reports every currently-spendable wallet for the given category (personal and/or company) so the client can present a choice when there is more than one. category is one of general/cafe/printing_internet/space_specific.

item.name: Availability (Calendar)
item.description: docs/decisions/booking-availability-and-calendar.md — the read side of the booking rules, powering the date picker and time-slot grid. Read-only and advisory: nothing here holds a slot, so POST bookings still re-checks under a row lock. Each slot's `reason` is the very message that endpoint would return for the same window, because both go through AvailabilityService.

item.name: Month Calendar — Which Days Are Open

query.description: Optional local date (Y-m-d). Defaults to the start of the current month.
Optional local date (Y-m-d). Max 62 days from `from`, else 422.

request.description: Day states for a date range: available | closed | full | past. A closed day carries `closed_banner` with its reason when a BusinessHourException gave one (a weekday with no schedule is closed with a null reason). A full day is OPEN but has no free slots, so it shows no banner. Also returns the branch-hours card, the legend and the rules block. Range capped at 62 days.

item.name: Day Slots — Times Free on a Date

request.description: The time-slot grid for one date. Each chip carries a state — available, booked, outside_hours, buffer, at_capacity, past — plus `is_available` and a translated `reason`. Slots are generated only inside the day's open periods, so a two-period day has no chips across the midday gap. `counts` summarises the grid.

query.description: Required. Local wall-clock time; a bare value means local, an explicit offset is honoured.

request.description: Powers the duration selector, computed end time, price and running total. The ladder comes from the booking.duration_options_minutes setting (seeded 60/90/120/180 = 1h/1.5h/2h/3h). An option that would run past closing, overlap a booking or break the space's granularity is returned with available:false and a stated reason rather than being hidden, so the app greys the chip out and can say why.

docs/decisions/booking-creation-approval-extension.md. Creates a confirmed+unpaid booking when the space has no wallet balance and requires_approval = false. 201 returns the created booking and auto-captures booking_id.

item.name: Create Booking — Error: Invalid Start Time

request.description: 422 `{"message": "The start time does not match this space's slot granularity."}`
422 `{"message": "This space is not available for the requested time."}` when a confirmed or pending booking already covers this window.

item.name: Create Booking — Error: Multiple Wallets, Choice Required

request.description: 422 `{"message": "More than one wallet can cover this booking. Please choose one.", "wallet_options": [...]}` when both a personal and a company balance apply -- resubmit with wallet_owner_type/wallet_owner_id from the list (see Wallet > Get Wallet Options).
Booking must already be checked in (checked_in_at set, checked_out_at null).
422 `{"message": "This booking cannot be extended past <latest_end_at>."}` when a confirmed or pending booking follows on the same space.

The member's own bookings with tab counts, following the {counts, data, meta} convention. `filter` splits on the booking's END time, so a booking under way still counts as upcoming. Each card carries `can_cancel`, driven by the exact predicate the cancel endpoint enforces.

item.name: Get Booking Detail — With Status Stepper

request.description: The detail screen: price breakdown, payment, note, and `request_status` — the Submitted → Under Review → Approved/Rejected stepper, derived from status and approved_at, never stored. A space that auto-confirms never had a review, so its stepper collapses to two steps. `actions.can_cancel` and `cancel_deadline_at` come from BookingCancellationService, so the button is never shown for an action that would 422. 403 for another member's booking.

Builds the confirmation screen WITHOUT creating anything: price breakdown (N hours × rate, subtotal, VAT from booking.vat_percent, total), the payment methods, and the note field. Every spendable wallet is listed — one that cannot cover the cost comes back with sufficient:false rather than being omitted — plus a synthetic `cash` option, which is what PaymentState::Unpaid plus reception settlement already means. `unavailable_reason` is the exact message POST bookings would return for the same window.

Self-service cancellation — the same BookingCancellationService reception calls. Refuses once the space's cancellation window has passed (422), after check-in (409), or for another member's booking (403). A wallet-paid booking is refunded to the member's personal wallet, and the slot is released.

The multi-select date strip: up to 10 windows, ALL OR NOTHING. Partial success would leave the member part-charged for a booking they never got, so any failure rolls the whole batch back and nothing is debited. Windows already accepted earlier in the same batch are checked against each other too. The wallet is debited ONCE for the summed total.

item.name: Create Booking — Batch Error: One Date Taken

request.description: 422 with a per-window `errors` array naming each bad window by its index in the submitted list, so the app can mark the offending chip. These two windows overlap EACH OTHER — neither is in the database yet, so a check against stored rows alone would pass both. Nothing is created.

item.name: Create Booking — Error: Start in the Past

request.description: 422 api.booking.start_in_the_past. Closes a trap where a past-dated booking could be created and paid for and then never cancelled, its cancellation window having long gone. A booking starting this very minute is still fine. Overridable via the booking.allow_past_bookings setting.

item.name: Kiosk
item.description: docs/decisions/kiosk-display.md. The member's app calls this after scanning the static QR the kiosk displays. It never creates a booking or session by itself -- it only queues a row on reception's screen, which reception confirms via Admin (Dashboard) > Reception Operations > Arrival Requests.

request.description: Matches the member's own booking for today at the (single) branch, if one exists with status confirmed/pending and no check-in yet -- purely informational, decides nothing. Calling this again while a request is still pending returns the existing row instead of creating a duplicate.

Returns the member Packages & Subscription screen data matching the mobile UI design.

Includes:
- Current plan card (name, active status, expiration date, renew CTA)
- Plan benefits (Cafأ©, Printing, Meeting rooms, Discounts)
- Granted wallet balances (Cafأ© balance, Printing balance with expiry)
- All available packages (Starter, Professional, Enterprise) with tags, prices, and Current Plan / Change Plan actions

response.name: 200 OK - Packages & Subscription

request.description: Gap found in the Task 15 Postman audit. Debits the buyer's personal wallet (or, with an optional company_id, the company's wallet -- requires CompanyPolicy::manageMembers) for plan.price and creates the Membership in one transaction. The plan must be a subscription (is_subscription = true) and currently active.

Updates the authenticated member's stored language preference (`ar`/`en`). Distinct from the `lang` header: the header overrides the response language for this one request; this changes what a future request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

Updates the authenticated member's stored currency preference (`USD`/`SYP`, display-only أ¢â‚¬â€‌ never affects real pricing/wallet records). Distinct from the `currency` header: the header overrides a plan-listing response's converted currency for this one request; this changes the stored default a request with no header falls back to. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success, not the updated user resource.

Returns the authenticated member wrapped inside `data.user`: account fields (id, name, phone, email, preferred_language, preferred_currency, status) plus `personal` (`bio`, `city`, `avatar_url`, `gender`), `professional` (`job_title`, `company_name`, `industry`), and `links` (`linkedin_url`, `instagram_url`, `behance_url`, `website_url`). Profile fields are null until the member has ever saved one. Also returns `completion` inside `data`: `score` (0-100) and `threshold` (from the `profile.completion_threshold` setting).

Upserts the personal AND professional profile in one call, in one transaction أ¢â‚¬â€‌ creates both rows on first call, updates them after, never a duplicate row on either table. Every field is optional and independently nullable: omitting a field leaves it unchanged, sending it as `null` explicitly clears it. Send every field together (as in this example) or just the subset you're changing أ¢â‚¬â€‌ both work. Plain single-language strings, not the `{ar, en}` bilingual JSON pattern used for admin-curated content. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success أ¢â‚¬â€‌ not the profile data, since you already sent it; use Get Profile to read it back.

Returns whether the authenticated member currently has an active `public_directory` consent grant: `{"granted": true|false}`. A member who never granted, or who revoked and never re-granted, gets `false`.

Grants (`granted: true`) or revokes (`granted: false`) the member's consent to appear in the public member directory (see Public (Site) أ¢â€ â€™ Get Member Directory). Consent is append-only history: granting while already active is a no-op, revoking sets `revoked_at` on the active row, and re-granting after a revoke inserts a fresh row rather than reusing the old one. Appearing in the directory also requires at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional) and an `active` account status. Returns `{"message": "..."}` on success أ¢â‚¬â€‌ use Get Consent Status to read the resulting state back.

Ingests a client-reported error/crash from the member mobile app. Lives under mobile.php, not member.php أ¢â‚¬â€‌ deliberately UNAUTHENTICATED (no bearer token needed): a crash can happen before login, e.g. on the splash/login screen itself, so this can't depend on a session existing yet. Placed here for discoverability alongside the rest of the mobile app's requests. Only `error_type` and `message` are required; everything else is optional context. `platform` is restricted to `android`/`ios`; `occurred_at` defaults to now() if omitted. Throttled at 60/min per IP. Returns a `message`-only body on success (201), not the created error-log resource.

item.name: Account
item.description: Delete is permanent and immediate. Deactivate is the reversible, self-service pause -- undo it with Auth/Account Reactivation (a WhatsApp code, since a deactivated account has no session to sign back into). Change Password is the authenticated alternative to Auth/Forgot Password, for a member who already knows their current password and is signed in; it proves identity with that password instead of a code, and only ends every *other* session, keeping this one alive.

request.description:
Voluntary, self-service pause -- the member's own counterpart to an admin deactivating/blocking a user (Admin (Dashboard)/Users/Update User Status). `reason` is optional free text, kept for the record. Every session this member holds is revoked, on every device.

Reversible only through Auth/Account Reactivation (a WhatsApp code) -- there is no way back in through Login while `deactivated`. An admin can also reverse it directly, same as a block. Returns `{"message": "..."}`, not the updated user resource.

The authenticated alternative to Auth/Forgot Password -> Auth/Reset Password: proves identity with `current_password` instead of a WhatsApp code, for a member who already knows it and is signed in. Same password rule as sign-up: min 8 chars, `confirmed`.

422 with `current_password_incorrect` if that field doesn't match -- the password is left unchanged.

On success, every OTHER session this member holds is revoked, but the one making THIS request stays alive -- unlike Reset Password, which ends all of them and issues nothing back. No new token is issued here either, since the current one is still valid; {{member_token}} keeps working as-is.

The example re-uses {{member_password}} for current and new so the variable stays valid for later requests in this collection -- swap in a real new value to test an actual change.

item.name: Access Control
item.description: QR-scan unlock (docs/decisions/qr-lock-unlock.md آ§4). A QR sticker fixed to the lock encodes devices.qr_value -- it only identifies which lock; the member's identity comes from their own session token, not from the QR itself.

request.description: Resolves qr_value to a lock, checks for an activated access_grants row for the scanning user (or a company they belong to with door_access_enabled) still inside its active window, and calls TTLockClient::remoteUnlock() server-side. Other denial responses not shown as saved examples: 404 `lock_not_found` (qr_value matches no lock), 503 `gateway_offline`/`unlock_failed` (the vendor call itself failed).

response.name: 403 Forbidden â€” No Active Grant

request.description: Returns paginated list of in-app notifications for the member, ordered by newest first.
Returns the unread notifications count for badge display in the mobile app.
Marks a single notification as read by its UUID.
Marks all unread notifications for the member as read in a single call.
Registers or refreshes the device FCM push token for multi-device push delivery (PRD 5.10).
Removes the device token upon logout. If body token is omitted, all tokens for the user are revoked.

query.description: تبويب الفعاليات: upcoming (الافتراضي) أو past أو all

request.description: جلب الفعاليات القادمة التي سجل فيها العضو الحالي. يعيد العدادات counts (مثل 3 upcoming)، معرّف التذكرة ticket_id، الشارات المزدوجة، وحالة التسجيل وزر View Ticket.
جلب الفعاليات السابقة التي سجل فيها العضو الحالي، مع حالة الحضور (Attended أو Missed) وزر View Event.

تسجيل العضو الحالي في الفعالية. تؤخذ بيانات العضو تلقائياً من حسابه (الاسم، البريد، الهاتف). في الفعاليات المجانية يتم التسجيل الفوري، وفي الفعاليات المدفوعة يتم خصم سعر الفعالية بالنقاط (price_points) مباشرة من محفظة العضو.

Always answers, even when the event asks nothing — `fields` is then [] and the app has one code path. `identity` carries the member's own name, phone and email as read-only: those are never asked again.
Answers are validated against the event's stored field definitions. Submitting name/phone/email is refused with 422 — they come from the token.
Most events need nothing the account does not already hold. An empty body is valid; check has_registration_form on the details endpoint first.

item.name: Admin (Dashboard)

request.description: Date bounds use min_date/max_date, not min/max: those hold numbers on every other type. Absolute YYYY-MM-DD only — "today" and "+30 days" are refused rather than half-supported.
Select and checkbox are refused without at least one option: an empty set would accept any value at submit time.
min/max on a checkbox bound how many boxes may be ticked.
`accept` takes a shorthand the server maps to mime rules; an unmapped value is logged and the constraint dropped rather than rejecting every upload.

`regex` takes a NAME, never an expression: alpha, alphanumeric, digits, email, url, syrian_phone, no_urls. A free-form pattern is refused — Laravel splits rule strings on |, so one could append rules to a member-facing validator, and a nested quantifier hangs the worker.
Omitting `validation` leaves the stored limits untouched; sending {} clears them.

docs/decisions/kiosk-display.md. One aggregate call for the reception kiosk screen: banner (one flat, mixed list of live Announcements, each item carrying its own `type` -- news/event/offer -- ordered by sort_order across all types together), plans (the active Plan catalog, its own top-level section, minimal shape -- no currency conversion; `name` is resolved to one string for the current `lang` header, unlike PlanResource's raw {ar,en} object), social_links (visible Contact Links, minimal shape), app_download.app_store / app_download.google_play and arrival_qr.value (Setting rows, editable via Admin > Settings -- the frontend renders the QR client-side from arrival_qr.value, this endpoint never generates an image). Every section key is always present, even as an empty array, so the kiosk app never has to guard against a missing key.
